utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we start, are there any matters that the parties would like to bring to the attention of this Bench? Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you. Yesterday as I understand that when Mr. Petrovic was testifying, Mr. Londrovic, the gentleman who had visited Mr. Petrovic down to try to get a statement from him with respect to Mr. Nikolic produced a statement that would seem to have been provided to him by the Office of the Prosecution regarding another investigation with respect to Muslim attacks and the killing of his father and brother. We have not been produced with that document. I don't know how it is that they, that is the Londrovic team was provided with that. I can only assume they were provided in order to establish motive, that if somebody lost a brother and a father, obviously they would want to kill Muslims if that person happened to be Serb. That must be the motive behind that. And I think, one, it is improper to be giving that sort of information to one counsel and not to others. Now, I understand it's another case, however, it impacts this case. And I think there is a sense of unfairness in this process. And perhaps that is why the Prosecution at times feels that I am attacking them. I am merely seeking the truth. I am not attacking anyone. But when they're going to produce documents for one side, they have to do it for other. I was totally unaware that Mr. Petrovic had ever been questioned by OTP because we were never provided with a statement. He was questioned about a totally different matter. I am not suggesting that they should not have produced it to Londrovic and company, in order so that they could shellac the witnesses the way they did yesterday. But it is fair game in this adversarial system, I guess, but if they're going to do it to one side, they have to give it to us as well. So I'm asking for that. The Prosecution anticipated my other request which was the production of the transcript. I appreciate it. I haven't had a chance to look it over, but I did read the pertinent part from [redacted]. So those are the two matters that I wish to bring at this point, Your Honour. And I would like to know whether the Prosecution is prepared to produce that document to us, that is, the Petrovic document. And I'll leave it at that for now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I believe that whenever you ask for a document, you have to show us the relevance of this document to this case. I don't think you elaborated too much on that point. I think that's the most important issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. How is it, Your Honour, how is it that Londrovic knew of this investigation that was done in the Muslim case? How is it that the Prosecution gives it to them in order for them to use it against Mr. Petrovic. How is it that when I indicated initially that I had a statement from Mr. Petrovic, we received a particular response to the Prosecution, which I'm prepared to read with respect to his comments, and that is: Almost to a single person in the VRS army has denied the Srebrenica incident. I think it's terribly important for us to have that. But aside from that, even if there's no linkage, what I'm doing here at every step of the way, and what I will continue to do, is show that the investigation in this case is not as objective as the Prosecution would want us to believe. I think I'm perfectly entitled to do that, because if they have pursued the investigation in a subjective manner, then obviously it calls into question, you know, what is available out there. Because we need to be mindful that there is no such thing in this Tribunal as equality of arms. There is none. And anybody who says that is absolutely talking nonsense. I don't have seven years to investigate a case. I don't have the resources. Unfortunately we have an adversarial system. We're not on a continental system where we have an objective, investigative Judge who is going to be investigating for both sides. However, I think it has been well said that the Prosecution in this case should behave and act as if they are the minister of justice. And so if they have those tools and those resources, they simply cannot, you know, look -- shy away from exculpatory information. This is part of my entire argument that they are engaging in tactics which I believe sometimes to be less than proper in getting to the truth. So I don't want to be sabotaged. I don't want to be engaged in guerilla warfare. I'm not suggesting we're there yet but we may be getting to that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I believe on your part you have to regard the intention of the other party with bona fide. Let me show you an example. Yesterday we conducted a closed session hearing our witness. It is the Prosecution who takes the initiative to ask for those transcripts to disclose to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour, however, the Prosecution was quite apt in pointing out that Karnavas would be asking for it. I'm grateful that he did that, but he knew that there would be an incoming request. And I'm not saying that he wouldn't have done otherwise, but all I'm suggesting, Your Honour, is that there was a strong reaction by the Prosecution when I first mentioned Petrovic. Nikolic, who's testified on their behalf, initially made a statement back in April. There has not been one single effort since then to contact Petrovic, not one single effort to contact [redacted]to see whether, you know, their versions of the event coincide with Nikolic. One would expect that the Prosecution, if they were so interested in the truth, that they would at least go back and say, "Hey [redacted], you never mentioned anything about this. What do you have to say? Mr. Petrovic, you're available, you're being accused of killing six people, what do you have to say?" No, it is the Defence that is going out there and doing that. And that's their attitude, the Defence can go out there and do it. All I'm suggesting is that when I see someone like Mr. Londrovic using a statement provided to them, it's like giving gasoline and saying pour it on the fire. It is a tactic which I would expect if I were back home in the United States, because it's more like a blood sport being in court. Unfortunately, that's what we have in the United States and that's not what we have here and that's not what I want to get into. We have different rules, different approaches. The courts here do not sanction the Prosecution. They do not -- they're not willing to keep evidence out if the disclosure material is late, because we cannot do that. I understand that. So the only tools that I have is my voice. The only tool is for me to jump up and ask for a bit of fairness. That's all I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, you have to understand that the Prosecution has the obligation to disclose any documents which might be favouring to your client. This is what the Rules say. But, on the other hand, Prosecution is not the investigators of your team. You have to understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And I hope you regard the intention of the other party with bona fide.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have thus far, Your Honour. I only call them into question when I think I need to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. McCloskey, do you think you could disclose that statement to Mr. Karnavas and to other Defence in this case?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No problem, Mr. President. Mr. Karnavas had asked me for that last night, of course I would have given it to him. I thought we had given it to everyone. Janet tells me we didn't. I can explain how those documents -- they resulted from, of course, the Court's request and I don't think it's appropriate for me at this point to go into it any more of that. I can talk to Mr. Karnavas off the record, as we do frequently, and talk about that. Regarding some of the other matters he mentioned, I think there was three or four allegations in there. I'm not going to get into that. I will just try to ignore it. If there is going to be attacks on the Prosecution, there should at least be a foundation for it. And I don't see any yet. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So, Mr. Karnavas, your request is granted. And by the way, could I ask you how long are you going to take to cross-examine the present witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I don't believe I'm going to take that long, but I do understand we don't have any other witnesses for the rest of the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I understand we don't have any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But that doesn't mean that you can prolong your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That wasn't my intention, Your Honour. I'm very mindful of the Court's time and I strive for efficiency and precision. I rarely hit the target, but I believe, based on my estimation, I should be through before the close of the first -- well, probably by the first break, one hour, maybe slightly less. I don't know. But I'll try to be efficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Karnavas, I understand you prepared very well for the cross-examination and your questions has some points in it. We appreciate your effort in this aspect. But sometimes your style, you add a lot of words, which we believe is not necessary in your question, which first, is easily to offend the other party; secondly, it will confuse the witness. Certainly sometimes you lose your point. So try to put the simplest question to the witness and try to avoid unnecessary conflictions between the parties in the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. I will try to limit my adjectives and adverbs and I'll take the admonition and work accordingly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, could we have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I apologise to you that you sat too long yesterday. I think you have to understand that you are a valuable witness and this Trial Chamber just wants to take advantage of your presence in The Hague to make better use of the time available. I hope you could understand that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I fully understand that. It wasn't really a problem. It was a bit strenuous, but it was all right in the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Are you ready to start, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning to you, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We left off yesterday while we were describing the location of the duty officer's room. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact, I believe you testified that from where you were located in the duty officer's room on that particular morning the way it's situated, you could not see who was walking into the building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, just to confirm that, I would like to show you what has been marked for identification purposes as D-70/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And accompanying with that, Your Honour, is D-70.1/1 and we have it translated. And I believe the D-70.1/1 gives an explanation as to where the diagram came from on page 2, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If you could look at the first two pages, which would be the ground floor with where it's marked 1 and 2 being on the far right and 4 and 3, what's marked as rooms 4 and 3 being on the far left. Could you please take a look at that. Do you see it? And if you just look at that ground floor and see if it fairly reflects the outline of that floor as you remember it or as it was, I should say, back then on July 1995. Is this a fair representation of it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under number 2 is the duty officer's room for the brigade, the operations room.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Right. And that's what I wanted to get to. So it is actually -- number 1 faces the gateway as you walk into the building. If you were in number 1 and you were looking outside the window, you would be facing the gateway, would you not? Room number 1.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not certain if there's a window in that room facing the gateway, room number 1, but I know that the entrance to the building faces the gateway.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And from room number 2 for certain, you could not see who was coming into the building if you were in that room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The narrow side, the flank of the building from the facade to the right of number 2, that's where the windows were. There are no windows on this side. There is only the door leading to another room, which was not the duty room.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So my answer -- my question is: Once you are inside the duty officer's room, you cannot see the way it's laid out, as it has been fairly depicted in this diagram, anyone coming into the building. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, when you got the call from Mr. Nikolic to replace him at 3.30, I take it you went into the duty officer's room, did you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you remained there until your shift was over?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And one of your duties is to answer the phone; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, while you were there from the period of 3.30 to 7.00, you never saw your commander, Colonel Blagojevic, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And he never called you, did he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm having a problem hearing, although I understand ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you never went to the commander's office, to your commander's office prior to taking your post -- prior taking over for Momir Nikolic, did you? In other words --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't go to the commander's office prior or after taking over.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm having some technical difficulties, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, would it be fair to say that you didn't know where your commander was at the time the telephone call came in at approximately 7.00 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where the commander was then, but Nikolic may have conveyed this to me orally when I was taking over from him. So perhaps I could have known, but I can't quite remember, so I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Are you suggesting that at 3.30 in the morning Mr. Nikolic would have conveyed to you that your commander is upstairs meeting with people at that hour of the night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible that he did. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Is there anywhere in your statement that you say that Nikolic gave you any instructions or gave you any information with respect to any meeting going on in the hours of 3.30 a.m. on that particular morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if he told me or not. His duty was to record all information that he had received in the duty operations book, logbook.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall ever reading in the duty operations book anything in there that Colonel Blagojevic was having a meeting at 3.30 in the morning or 4.30 in the morning or 5.30 in the morning or 6.30 in the morning or 7.00 while you were sitting there filling in for Momir Nikolic? And it's yes or it's no. Not a maybe. Do you recall ever seeing anything of the sort?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Objection, Your Honour, demanding a yes or no question is not a fair way to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's cross-examine, Your Honour. It's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I understand. But you have to lay some foundations if there's a meeting there or there's an allegation of the meeting between 3.00 to 7.00, then you ask this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know whether a meeting was scheduled, sir, at 3.30, 4.30, 5.30, 6.30 or 7.00 in the morning at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters while you were filling in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know whether any meeting was supposed to be held, especially at that time during the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And once you got -- before you went to take up and fill in for Momir Nikolic as duty officer, you did not see any officers coming in, including your commander, Colonel Blagojevic. Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You didn't see any high-ranking officers coming in that night -- those early hours. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't see anyone entering the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. So as you sit here today, as you sit here today, you cannot point to anything concrete that would help us and help you verify that Colonel Blagojevic was inside -- upstairs in his office conducting a meeting with people from up there, can you, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have nothing related to that. I didn't see anyone, therefore I can't say who was where at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, we're going to get to the intercept, but first I want to discuss a little bit about your interview with respect to the intercept. As I understand it, when you were questioned by the Prosecution they had suggested, as a result of the conversation that took place with the intercept, that you were coordinating, that the police were coordinating the refugees being evacuating. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. When you were speaking with the Prosecutor, did there not come a time when he asked you or that he said that the police were coordinating it and telling the General -- telling the -- that the police were coordinating the evacuation process, meaning that the military police were coordinating the evacuation process. Do you recall the Prosecutor telling you that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall him telling me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, if you could look at page 83. It might be at the bottom of page 82, actually in your -- but I'm going to read on, from page 83, line 1 to 2. But you may want to look at the last two lines of the previous page, and for the English version it will be page 82, line 21, and I'm reading from your statement which has been marked for identification purposes as D-68/1. And if you could read to yourself first all the way to perhaps line 11 on page 83, from 1 to 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. In the English, I'm --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In the English it's page 82, starting with line 21 going all the way to page 83, to line 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you see that? Do you see that, sir, where there's a suggestion by the Prosecutor --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact, you correct him and you tell him that you were not coordinating. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. You don't need to look at the statement anymore. I'm just going to ask you a few questions. And in fact during that exchange, he had suggested that you were coordinating because you were a commander of the -- or the chief of the military police, and you were having a conversation with a general with respect to the evacuation. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And at that point, you told him that you were not coordinating but you were merely having this conversation as a result of a telephone call coming in into the duty office while you were the duty officer. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that you were not responding to the general in your capacity as the chief of the military police, but rather, in your capacity as the duty officer. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And so had you been, for instance, the deputy assistant of logistics or the chief engineer of the engineering department, at that moment in time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, the issue is very clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You don't have to confuse the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now -- and then at some point Mr. McCloskey who had come into the court, into the room --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm going to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Again, we're going back to going over a statement. This witness, I believe, will answer the questions and probably say what he said before, but just going over the statement is really not relevant unless this witness can't answer or doesn't remember, and that hasn't been established. It would be much quicker if he would ask the questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Up to now I believe that Mr. Karnavas did pretty good.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But I don't know what the following question is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We don't know because I haven't asked it. And I don't see, unless he's clairvoyant, Your Honour, how he can know. Right now I'm going into the aspect of "up there," that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Karnavas, try to ask a direct question to this witness and do not involve the other party if unnecessary in your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is necessary because it is the Prosecutor himself who is asking these questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Everybody knows because we got transcripts. You don't have to emphasise this point. Just put the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, it's for the witness's benefit, Your Honour, but okay, very well, I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You then had -- you were then asked about -- you were asked to give an interpretation of this intercept. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And your interpretation then was different from your interpretation in this courtroom. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because maybe -- well, it is my opinion that in the translation itself -- you see, because I believe that in our language, like in any other language, it is very important where there is a period where there is a comma, so punctuation can change the meaning of a sentence, if you follow what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I follow precisely, because that's what I want to ask you next. Did you hear your voice, so you can connect the voice of what you -- assuming that you had this conversation and assuming that you said those things, did you hear your voice to see whether a period should be placed where it was placed by whoever was listening in to that conversation? Did you hear a tape recording?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not hear my voice. I got this conversation on paper in my own language, while the investigators, the Prosecution, they were looking at the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Just a moment. So you didn't put that period there yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've just said, I don't know whether you heard me because it seems that your headphones weren't working properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I did. So it's fair to say that whoever was listening in chose to put a period there, as opposed to, say, a comma or just a pause. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Probably the person who was translating that could translate -- well, that's why I'm saying it. There can be several different ways of interpreting this, depending on how it is put.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Exactly. And since we don't have a tape recording of what exactly you said, as you stand here today, given your memory, can you give us any assurances that those were the exact words that you had said on that morning at 7.00 a.m. when the telephone came in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have said already in Banja Luka that I cannot remember that conversation at all. I did not remember that anyone called me. How can I know who called me and what I said so many years ago?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. If somebody was up, for instance, at Pribicevac, the third -- the forward command post of the 3rd Battalion, would you say that they're up there? "Gore."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Pribicevac is dominant. It's a high elevation, so it is up there, I mean -- well, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Let me move on to another subject. We talked yesterday about you having to provide security for Mladic and others.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, it is your understanding and your belief that you had approximately 30 men in total. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And there was a certain number of people that you needed to conduct day-to-day tasks that were required of the military police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In other words, some had to stay at the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And of course when someone like Mladic would come in, you would have to provide security for them. That's one of the tasks that is required. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the command post and the entrance into the brigade headquarters that were secured. As for his movement, all of his movements were secured by the military police. So then I did not have to know whether he came to brigade headquarters, because when he came to brigade headquarters, the military police came with him. And if he left the brigade headquarters and went out into the field, they went with him yet again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And when they were with him, were they not under his command and control?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And if he wanted to say, once in Potocari, to ask them to perform certain tasks, would they not be required to do so, to do those tasks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he didn't have to look for me and to say, give orders to the policemen to do this and that. No way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And I take it they -- your military police didn't have the authority to tell Mladic that he couldn't give them an order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even the corps commander or the commander of the brigade did not dare say anything like that to him, let alone me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And in fact you had seen him kick in a rear a lieutenant colonel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So you don't know exactly what Mladic might have done or what orders he might have given to your military police officers once they were with him in Potocari, do you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were assigned to guard him personally, to provide security for him personally. He could have chased them away, told them not to guard him at all. He could have done whatever he wanted to do. That was his right. I could not interfere. The commander couldn't interfere, the corps commander, no one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And some of your men, as I understand it, were being directly ordered by Nikolic himself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And some, as I understand it, were being ordered by Popovic himself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And it would appear, it would appear, that nobody was coming to Mr. -- to you to ask you for your permission or to give you the -- to provide you with the information as to what your men would be doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was perhaps a bit above an ordinary soldier, but that was not the practice. I really don't know whether they were duty-bound to do that or not. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, when Mladic travelled, would he announce in advance where he would be going to the military police so they could provide him an escort or, say, drive down a road to see that it's protected?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, sometimes, for instance -- well, I don't know who asked when he went to Pribicevac, but perhaps it was Popovic and Nikolic, too, who said that General Mladic would be going up there and that there are people are escorting him, the military police travelling with him, with him personally, and providing security for him himself and then there would be this other matter of sending a patrol that would be lined up along on the road at certain intervals because there was thick vegetation, thick forest on both sides, so this road went through the forest. Then it was this road that was supposed to be secured as much as possible. It's a long road. I don't even know how many kilometres there are there. You would need a battalion perhaps, or even more than that to provide security there. Then again, if someone wanted to liquidate someone, they could I think because it's such a long road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What if he was going to go to Konjevic Polje, would he tell you to provide security in advance, to make sure everybody knew exactly what his travel plans were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one knew what his travel plan was. He could decide on that -- on his own and now he would think this and then he would think that, whatever would come into his mind, he would simply go and do it. But the road to Konjevic Polje was not guarded by the military police, the road itself, because there were troops, some troops belonging to the Army of Republika Srpska along that road. But military police travelled with him, escorted him. It was a Puch vehicle, and the military police escorted him in a Pinzgauer, I think. So they moved along with him. They were not guarding the road from Bratunac to Konjevic Polje, it's 22 kilometres. Can you imagine how many soldiers would be required to provide adequate security along that road?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would the military police that were with him call in at least to the headquarters, the military police headquarters, to let you or your deputy and others know where they were on the road at any given time, so at least you would know that your men are with Mladic heading towards Konjevic Polje, heading towards Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They didn't even have any means of communication, any communication device, so they could not inform the command of the brigade, the brigade headquarters or me personally. And it wasn't their duty either because General Mladic probably wouldn't have allowed them to do that. He didn't want to be held accountable to anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Why was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Because he was the highest ranking officer. Why would he tell the brigade commander or the commander of the military police or whoever anything?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Could that also not compromise his own security if he telegraphed to everybody where he would be going?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, possibly it could. I don't know. He's the one who decided about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, Mr. Nikolic has testified that on the afternoon of the 13th he learned when he got to the military police headquarters that Mladic would be going off to Konjevic Polje and as a result of that he took a drive down there to make sure that the road was secure for the commander to be -- to come through, the commander of the Main Staff. Now, do you recall knowing anything about Mr. Mladic or General Mladic telling you or telling others at the headquarters of the military police that he was going down -- he would be going down towards Konjevic Polje in the afternoon or around noon time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know how it was. A telephone could be made or a courier could come and say six men are required, six policemen are required to provide security for Mladic, and automatically six policemen would go. And not at any point in time was it said where they would go. So they went. They did provide security for him, but where they would go with him, they didn't know. For as long as he would not say, "I don't need you anymore," they would have to be with him. If he would say, "You're off. You can go now," then they would go back to the police, but in the meantime they were at his disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But you don't recall whether everybody in the Bratunac Brigade headquarters knew at sometime on the 13th, around noon-ish, 1.00 or so, that Mladic would be going through to Konjevic Polje, because that's what Nikolic says, that he came and he learned it from y'all and then he went to make sure that the road was secure and safe for the general to travel. Does that sound logical to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. The military police could not know before Nikolic knew. The military police could not know. He could not have said to the military police, I would go to such and such a place when he had his own security man, or rather, the security man of the Main Staff. He could tell him everything. "I will go, you organise whatever." That's the way it is. I don't know that he announced going there at all. I think that he -- they escorted him all the way to Han Pijesak, the military police of the Bratunac Brigade. I think they said that he stopped somewhere and that they filled up the Pinzgauer tank, because it uses up a lot of gasoline, and then they accompanied him all the way up there. And where he exactly went, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Up there. That's what I meant. Okay. I was making a reference to "gore" because you didn't mention the place. You said "up there," as if that's -- in your language, when you're referring to a place that's sort of up on the hill, you would say "gore"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to switch to another topic. When you were

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: of questions regarding I believe it was the 13th of July. And you were, asked if you knew Nenad Djokic and if you knew Nenad Deronjic. Do you recall that series of questions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: And you were asked whether you were aware that according -- that there was a Muslim survivor near Konjevic Polje who had indicated that approximately 16 Muslim prisoners were executed by the banks of a particular river, the Nadja -- Jadar River. Do you recall that, being asked those questions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall that.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: For the record I'm referring to the transcript, if the Prosecutor wants to check, it's on page 82. Now, my question is: When you met with the Prosecutor on Sunday to be briefed, to be prepared for here, did he present you with anything to show you that you were at that vicinity of the events when they occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The event that had to do with the killing, is that what you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: Right. My question is: Did he show you anything that would give you at least some assurances that you were in or around the area where those people were taken and then executed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said myself that I was there in Konjevic Polje. Now, nothing was shown to me that would prove that I was there precisely at that time, because I said in which period I was there. Now, it did not have to mean that it was done precisely when I was there. It didn't mean that it was precisely at that place. I was at the crossroads and Konjevic Polje is a village, a settlement which has a rather big area. And then there's the river. It's -- a river flows and it can be a kilometre upstream, a kilometre downstream. How should I know. I just said that I didn't see this and I can't say anything about it. How could I?

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: Okay. Well, he says here: "A kilometre or two on the banks of the river." So as I understand, you were on the road primarily and as far as you are aware, you didn't see any such events?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that we were at the crossroads itself. I said where we went. I said we were moving towards Bratunac in the direction of Bratunac behind that vehicle, so this has already been said.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: All right. But I want to make sure -- my question is: Did he show you anything that would give us the impression that you would have knowledge of that event, because you were watching it. You were seen watching it. There's some physical evidence, something, anything, that would give us the impression that somehow you were connected or you were aware of this incident.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't see anything and nothing was shown to me, no document or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: Okay. I want to move to another topic. Yesterday you were asked a question with respect to Radenko Zaric. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: All right. Do you know the gentleman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: All right. Now, just out of curiosity, before coming yesterday into court while you were meeting with the Prosecution being prepared, did the Prosecution ever share with you the statement that they had from Mr. Zaric?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Mr. Zaric's statement was never shown to me.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: Did they ever share with you what they knew of what Mr. Zaric had told them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I was told in the courtroom. I was told that Zaric had stated that I had sent him to Potocari to --

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: I'm asking you before coming to the courtroom, did they give you an opportunity and did they tell you what Zaric had said and give you an opportunity to provide them with an answer? I don't see it in the proofing notes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we didn't discuss that. This was not mentioned. I think we only talked about that here in the courtroom, that's why I'm saying this, but not before.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: Okay. And as also I -- very well. (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted).

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: Well, what was Mr. Jovanovic's position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was -- before me, he was the commander of the military police, and then he was transferred to -- I don't know -- there are certain distinctions to be drawn there, but I can't quite -- chief of security with the Bratunac Brigade staff, that was Nikolic. Now, there was something concerning intelligence. I can't quite remember the exact term, what the position was called exactly, but he was based in an office, together with Nikolic. So again, he had to do with the police.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: Okay. Where Mr. Nikolic in his testimony indicated that Mr. Jovanovic was not there, was not -- was outside the Bratunac area during these critical periods, yet Mr. Zaric says that he believes he saw Mr. Jovanovic in Potocari on that day. Do you have a comment about that? You've got one Prosecution witness saying he's no where near the area. You've got another witness saying he's in Potocari. Do you recall seeing Mr. Jovanovic there that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where he was, where Jovanovic was on that day. I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, at some point he's asked, Mr. Jovanovic [sic] in his statement, he's asked about how many people went up to Potocari. And he states, everybody in the military --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think he's got the names mixed up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: I was just corrected improperly so. Mr. Zaric is asked during his interview, and I'm reading from page 6. From his interview he's asked: "And when you were deployed to the enclave, who was deployed with you?" And on page 7, lines 1 all the way down through 4 he says: "So all of us, everybody in the military police. I think about 20 of us were all deployed in that area." And the next question is: "Were you all summoned to one central point before being deployed and given a briefing?" And his answer is: "No." So he seems to think that everybody, and then he qualifies it to about 20 people in the military police being summoned and told to go to Potocari. As I understand your testimony, yesterday you said you did not issue such orders. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: And as I further understand you, given the size of your platoon, the military police platoon of the Bratunac Brigade, and given the day-to-day tasks, including providing security for Mladic, this would have been an impossibility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely. This would have been impossible. There were other ongoing activities. This number as specified, 30 people, we were all there, we were all on the list, the 30 of us. 10 people remained for all the other activities, the checkpoint, guarding the bridge, guarding the members of the Dutch Battalion, securing the wounded who were at the clinic, at the health centre, securing the command post, guarding the military police building, personal security for General Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: Now, in this -- Mr. Zaric says that a car was sent to pick him up at home because he was -- he had a day or two off. Were there a lot of military police officers that had days off during those days or was everybody deployed because of the circumstances?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because of the circumstances, no one was allowed to leave the unit. Someone may have been sick or a family member may have been sick. But the person would only have been allowed to leave briefly for a day or two maybe, even in that case.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to switch to another topic, and that is dealing with the security of the schools in Bratunac or where the Muslim prisoners were detained. As you might recall, yesterday we talked about -- there was some questions posed to you by the Prosecutor. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: And you told us that you received an order by Mr. Nikolic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: Now, when Mr. Nikolic gave you the order, he did not say that this order was coming from the commander, your commander, Colonel Blagojevic, did he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He didn't tell me where the order had come from, nor was he duty bound to tell me about that, who he had received his order from.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: All right. Did he tell you exactly how many men you had to provide?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: Did he tell you that it was your -- your responsibility, that is, the responsibility of the military police platoon of the Bratunac Brigade to guard all those prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I didn't understand the question. (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted).

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He didn't say that it was my responsibility. He said I should send people over there to help because there were very few soldiers there. I'm not sure from whose unit, that assistance should be provided for them in carrying out security tasks there.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: All right. And he did not tell you that those prisoners belonged to and were under the control of the Bratunac Brigade, did he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't. He didn't say. It was under the control of the Army of Republika Srpska. Now, which particular unit -- very many units took part in that operation from all over the place, all sorts of units, but only the Bratunac Brigade could have done this job.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: All right. And you said that Mladic was there with his forward command post at the Hotel Fontana only a few hundred metres away. Right

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The testimony was that Mladic was in Han Pijesak at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll rephrase, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: You indicated that Mladic's forward command post, the command post of the Main Staff of the VRS army, was located during that period in time in the Hotel Fontana, only a few hundred metres away from where these prisoner were being detained. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: And is your understanding that the Drina Corps forward command post during those days was also at that same hotel, Hotel Fontana?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: And of course we have Colonel Beara running around Bratunac. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure if he was running around Bratunac, but I do know that he was part of the Main Staff that was based at the Fontana Hotel.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: And you know Popovic was there and giving orders to your men. Right, from the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: And you saw Nikolic with Beara and Popovic together?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This may be a good time to take a break, Your Honour. I don't have too much more, I think 15 more minutes perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll break now and we'll resume until quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: Now, before we get on to the next subject, I just want to ask you one question. It's my understanding that in your statement to the Prosecution you had indicated that the Bratunac Brigade military police were not coordinating and not communicating -- or not communicating, I should say, with MUP. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted).

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you were asked some questions about Pilica; do you recall that, yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: And it's been established that two members of the Bratunac Brigade military police were in Pilica. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how many there were, whether two or a different number.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: Okay. But they said -- they used the word "patrol," and that was, I believe, your understanding and that that would constitute two police officers, two military police officers. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: And if I understand your testimony from yesterday, you don't know how they got there. In other words, who ordered them to be there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: And in fact you did not know at the time that they were up there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know because I wasn't there myself. I went to the other village that I talked about.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: And it was later on that you learned they had been up there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when I learned.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: Did you ever hear that your -- anybody under your command had committed any atrocities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware of anything like that.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: All right. Did you ever try to find out how it was or who it was that ordered those two or that patrol of the Bratunac Brigade military police to be up in Pilica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who ordered them, nor did I ever try to find out who did.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: All right. Now, Mr. Nikolic indicated when he entered into an agreement with the Prosecution, he had indicated certain things that made it into the newspaper in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Do you recall reading some things that were stated by Mr. Nikolic in his statement of facts and acceptance of responsibility before this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. I have a copy of the article from the newspaper when the statement was published.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: All right. And I take it you read that statement, did you not? You read the article?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can even show my copy to the Honourable Chamber, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: All right. And was that printed about the time that Nikolic entered into this agreement? Would that have been around April or May of this year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly when it was published, whether it was before or after his agreement with the Office of the Prosecutor. I do know that it was published. That's all I know. Whether it was before of after, I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: And do you happen to have it here in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: Right now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: Okay. You don't mind sharing it with us. If I could take a look at it real quickly. All right. If we could put it on the ELMO for just a second. Let me just ask him a couple of questions regarding that. Okay. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll be asking that that be moved into evidence, Your Honour, if we could make a copy at some point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, do you have the translation of this article?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I don't have the translation, but I'm prepared to ask some questions, just some foundational questions, and then at some point we can have the article translated. But I'm not going to go into depth -- into the content of the article itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, as the extraordinary case, we will allow you to do that. But just remember, we will not accept any documents which we don't understand at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour. And I'm improvising at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Let's see how far you can go with this article.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: Now, if you could look at the top of the article, sir, take a look at the top of it, and please tell us the date.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What it says here is the following: "The subject, daily Avaz, 8th of May, 2003."

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: Okay. 8th May, 2003. Now, since that time, sir, has the Prosecution contacted you to get your account of what Mr. Nikolic had said with respect to Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, although I expected to be contacted by the Office of the Prosecutor and be invited to give my account, but I was never called before I got the date, the 22nd of October 2003, to appear here before the Court.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: Were you in Bratunac this entire period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: Were you in hiding or were you -- could you be seen in case somebody wanted to contact you?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. This appears to -- I don't understand the relevance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The relevance is quite obvious, Your Honour. Had the Prosecution wished to contact him he was available. He was not in hiding and he was within their grasp and reach.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, we don't think this question is necessary. The point is very clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I wasn't sure, Your Honour. I wasn't sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We are sure.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: Now, you were invited, were you not, by the police department of the Bratunac municipality to give a statement, were you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: Were you provided with the statement that they had prepared as a result of the statement -- as a result of your conversation with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: Now, I happen to have a copy of it and if I may share it with you. And this would be D-71 -- D-71/1 for identifications purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It has not been translated, Your Honour. We just received this by fax, but I have a way of getting what it is that we need to get out of this statement. I will have it translated at some point.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: Now, sir, if you could just look at it and see whether you recognise this.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: [redacted] And the Prosecutor asked me to bring it along, so I have. I have it here with me. I've brought it today. I managed to locate it and I brought it to court today. I'm familiar with this statement because I received this statement immediately after I had given the interview.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: All right. So the statement I've handed you is identical to the one you just pulled out of your pocket?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: Okay. Very well. Now, if you could look at the third page, the third page and if I could ask you to read so we can get a translation of the very last paragraph on this statement. If you can just read it and we'll get a translation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I also wish to state that I had the opportunity of reading the text of the alleged statements made by Nikolic, Momir, in newspapers such as Dnevni Avaz and other newspapers, and I did not recognise as true the statement presented in these newspapers, because what was presented in the newspapers was completely false, in my opinion, as well as inaccurate information given about me and other persons named in the text. So I cannot accept this statement as truthful.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Do you know whether during this period of time from May until today, whether Mr. Petrovic was in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: And of course he gave a statement as well, as you well know. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He gave a statement on that same day. I've said that it was the same day when I was there, but he was there before me. It says here -- I beg your pardon. It says here -- I didn't even see it before. I mean, I don't remember seeing it. I saw it last night when I was looking for this document when I came from this court. I saw that it says here quite nicely what the date is and also on the top it says: "Started at 1240 hours." And at the end it says: "The statement taking was completed at 1430 hours." So the time is there, how long the statement was taken.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: All right. Now, as I understand it, you began your career as a police officer. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: And in fact you were a police officer were several years before you became -- you switched careers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: All right. Given your background and experience, given your background and experience, do you not think that it would have been appropriate for the Prosecutor to come down to Bratunac and to take a statement from Mr. Petrovic as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection to relevance, Your Honour. Unless -- if the Prosecution has been established to be on trial here, I would like to know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: They are.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I don't think he's established one width of evidence and -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey. I quite agree with you. Mr. Karnavas, I warned you before the start of the trial about that. It's not necessary. Do not involve the other parties unless you have some concrete specific case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic was available during this entire period in Bratunac, had the Prosecutor wanted to contact him and take a statement. Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could have taken a statement from me and from Petrovic and from many other persons who were there. I don't know. I don't know about anybody hiding any of the people who are mentioned.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, yesterday I began by asking you and pointing out that section where you believed Mr. Petrovic to be a good man, an honest man, conscientious and so on. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: Now, as you know, he lost some members of his family during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he lost his brother. I don't know whether he lost any other family members.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR HERE THE
utterances.text: But isn't it a fact, sir, that as long as you have known him, as long as you have known him, and while he served with you with the Bratunac Brigade in the military police, that he always conducted himself correctly. Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may have just one second, Your Honour. (redacted). (redacted). (redacted).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, you have to understand this witness is under the protective measures. There were several occasions that you accidentally mentioned something which might disclose the identity of this witness. Could we go into the private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: (redacted).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When we looked at yesterday's transcript of this witness's testimony, it seemed to us that we had a few things that needed clarification. So, Your Honour, those are the only questions we have. I don't think we have anything that would be relevant to our defence otherwise.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could we please just clarify some things that could be important. Yesterday and today in response to -- or rather yesterday, in response to the Prosecutor's questions, you said when speaking about the 14th of July, 1995, that you got orders from Popovic and Major Nikolic to help with the escort of Muslim prisoners to Zvornik. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Also, you said that this was sometime around 10.00?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And then you went on to say that you were in this column with an APC and that the column was being lined up behind you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we still have time, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That a few times you moved the APC so that the column could be lined up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That at one point in time they walked up to you and asked you whether you were supposed to tank up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was where the road forks off towards the headquarters of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The microphone was not on. The microphone is still not on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Your microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And finally, you left around 1330 hours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I filled up, then I moved yet again, then we waited there for a while. I don't know for how long, perhaps about 1.30 or 2.00 we left from that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That is precisely the fact we wanted to clarify, so around 1.30 or 2.00 you set out for Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What is the distance between Bratunac and Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Bratunac to Zvornik the distance is registered as being 43 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So this kind of column on that day, the 14th of July, 1995, how much time did you need to cover these 43 kilometres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since this was a column, it could not move fast, although it did not stop on the way. So the tempo of the movement of this column was dictated by Colonel Popovic. He was at the head of the column with this vehicle of his. I apologise to the interpreters again for fiddling with the microphone. So all the vehicles had a proper distance between each other. So we were moving along that way. I don't know at which speed really, because I was driving this vehicle and I wasn't really looking, but the speed on that particular vehicle is shown in miles. But most probably, I don't think that the column could be moving even at 40 kilometres per hour, so perhaps it needed about an hour, an hour and a half to get there, because it even went on further, so these are narrow roads.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If I draw the right conclusion, that would mean that you would have reached Zvornik around 1430 hours or 1500 hours on that day, the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, around that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And you said that you did not stop in front of the headquarters of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not. We did not stop anywhere until that school. I just stopped by a bridge on this road when one turns towards the village of Sapna because this was a narrow, concrete bridge and I wasn't sure, I couldn't assess from that vehicle, whether I could safely cross this bridge. I did not know how it was constructed, this concrete construction, and of course how wide it was, because the vehicle itself is rather wide.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So you were in front of that school around 1500 hours or 1530 hours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, around that time. We probably needed about an hour and a half to get there. Perhaps it was 1500 hours, perhaps 1530 hours, because we were moving very slowly along this narrow road. We moved very slowly from the fork off near Karakaj to the left. And then after this wider road, we turned to the right, again a narrower road which is not as wide as the other one that goes from Karakaj itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see whether there were any prisoners who had been brought to that school before you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see any prisoners in the school, because of course I did not even enter the school. I did not get out of the APC. But it is my assumption that there was no one there in that school, that the school was empty.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So in this context let us take care of one thing. It is possible that a similar convoy of the same size left from Bratunac on that same morning and went there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Perhaps it could have gone early in the morning, but again I'm telling you, perhaps around 10.00, 9.30. As I said, I was parked at the crossroads at around 10.00 near the bus station. So at that time no one could have passed there. And I think that not a single convoy left before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Further on you said that during this journey all the time, and on the basis of the information that was given to you by Major Nikolic, it was said that these people were going for an exchange?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Not at a single moment -- I mean, I said this because I knew this. It was logical to me. They said that many of our people stayed behind in Tuzla, and I have to point this out here before the Court. In Tuzla, the population did not have very strong ethnic feelings, generally speaking, throughout the territory of Tuzla. When speaking of Bosnia-Herzegovina and all of the former Yugoslavia, when people voted for national parties, it was only in Tuzla in that the reformist forces won the election, whereas in all other bigger towns and cities, the nationalist parties one. So that is why a lot of people stayed there. People did not move out of the territory of the municipality of Tuzla. Many people of Serb ethnicity remained in the territory of the municipality of Tuzla. They stayed on there. They lived there. Then after the 15th of May when at Brcanska Malta those soldiers were killed, and then Tuzla was blocked, sealed off, and then people could no longer get out of Tuzla. And it seemed logical to me that now, perhaps it was somebody's decision, that these people from Srebrenica would be exchanged for the people who were there and who wanted to get out of Tuzla, who were blocked in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So there was no reason, there were no grounds for any one of you who was escorting this convoy could conclude what would happen to the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no one could conclude what would happen to the prisoners. It's nonsense. I mean, how could anyone think that? This is what seemed logical and I said that it was logical, that these people would be taken to the area that was under the control of their forces and the people who wanted to get out of this territory because they were blocked, of course they could not leave, and that then they could go to the territory they wanted to go to. If they didn't want to go, of course nobody could coerce them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Just another question. As you were headed for the school once you turned off from the Zvornik/Bijeljina road, did you perhaps notice another crossroads with a fountain nearby?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that particular crossroads.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions. Thank you

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any re-direct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just a few questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Witness, do you recall telling the Office of the Prosecutor in your interview in Banja Luka that you had seen Mr. Beara in the Bratunac Brigade compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did see him in the compound of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you tell us, was that before or after the fall of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if it was before or after the fall. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you see him in the compound after the fall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I don't know whether I saw him before or after the fall of Srebrenica. At any rate, he was there always. He was moving about the area, the Bratunac area. He was based at the Fontana Hotel. It's possible that he came over, but I can't be sure as to when exactly I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But did he come over to the Bratunac Brigade compound frequently during this time period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not frequently, no. Not frequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How often would you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how often. I can't answer your question accurately. It's difficult to say.
